section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions how the renewal of the month, which indicates miraculous renewal through one's own effort, relates to the year, which indicates constancy and natural order.
section.t: However, it still needs to be understood what is written, "It is the first for you for the months of the year,"
that the concept of the month
(the Rosh Chodesh of redemption)
which indicates renewal
(a miraculous conduct that comes through the renewal of service with one's own power)
also relates to the year, which indicates constancy and the absence of change and renewal
(a natural conduct that was established at the beginning of creation).

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that all aspects of the chain of descent depend on the service of Israel, and even the natural order was created for the sake of the future service of the righteous.
section.t: The explanation of this is,
that, behold,
ultimately, all the matters in the chain of descent depend on the service of Israel, and they are for the sake of Israel,
meaning,
that even the natural conduct as it was established at the beginning of creation is for the sake of Israel,
and as it is brought in Rashi's commentary on the verse,
"In the beginning, G-d created..."
"For the sake of Israel, who are called 'beginning'."
And this is what is written,
"With the king in his work, they sat there,"
and our sages said,
"Whom did He consult? The souls of the righteous."
That is, He contemplated the souls of Israel
(as they would be in the future)
and created the world.
And as the Mitteler Rebbe wrote in Or HaTorah,
that the precedence of the will was so that there would be righteous Jews in every generation, and He, so to speak, contracted His radiance,
like the parable of a father who contracts his intellect and speaks childish words for the sake of his young son,
and also all the attributes of youthful actions are born in the father.
However, below, the son must first exist,
and afterwards the father can contemplate him, etc.,
but regarding the Holy One, blessed be He, the past and the future are equal before Him,
and He, may He be blessed, took delight from the deeds of the righteous
(that would be in the future)
and contracted Himself, etc.
However, before creation, the delight from the deeds of the righteous was in potential,
and afterwards
(when He chose Yaakov and his sons and gave them the Torah)
the deeds of the righteous
(service with one's own power)
needed to be in actuality,
and for this was the intention of creation.
And it is found,
that even the order of natural conduct
(year)
depends on the service of Israel,
and this is the matter of "This month is for you,"
"Since He chose Yaakov and his sons..." the Rosh Chodesh of redemption,
which is the renewal of the Giving of the Torah,
that the Torah descended below into this physical world,
meaning it penetrated even into the matters below in this physical world,
that even the aspect of natural conduct depends specifically on the service of Israel.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section distinguishes between the service that sustains natural conduct and the service that elicits miraculous conduct, based on the simple and deeper interpretations of the verse "If you walk in My statutes."
section.t: However, nevertheless there is a difference between the service that is for the sake of natural conduct,
and the service upon which miraculous conduct depends.
And the explanation is,
for it is written,
"If you walk in My statutes and keep My commandments and do them, then I will give your rains..."
And the simple explanation, as it is in the Written Torah
("A verse does not depart from its simple meaning")
is that "If you walk in My statutes" refers to the study of Torah in its simple sense,
and "keep My commandments" refers to the fulfillment of the commandments in general,
and then the reward, "I will give your rains in their time... and the tree of the field will give its fruit," is also in its simple sense,
meaning,
a natural reward.
And above this,
according to the explanation in the Oral Torah, in which the true will of the Supernal One is revealed,
as it is stated in the Toras Kohanim
(and brought in Rashi)
that the explanation of "If you walk in My statutes" is
(not just the study of Torah in general,
but rather)
that you should toil in Torah,
which is the matter of exertion in Torah beyond one's nature and habit.
And since "study is great because it leads to action,"
meaning,
that the toil in Torah is for the sake of observing and fulfilling,
then also "keep My commandments" is
(not just the fulfillment of the commandments in general,
but rather)
the fulfillment of the commandments with beautification, etc.
And then the reward is also in a miraculous manner, above nature,
"I will give your rains in their time,"
specifically on Wednesday nights and Shabbos nights,
"and the tree of the field will give its fruit,"
that even barren trees will produce fruit.
